doc.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013

title: Getting arrangements played by Basie and the Basie sound
summary: Gardner explains the band's strict standards for new charts, the Basie arrangers, and how Basie would carve up arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: But did you eventually get — you wrote something and then the band played it?

Oh no. That didn’t happen for maybe another two years from the first time I went to the front of the bus and showed Fos my arrangement, you know. And that was like passing out an arrangement to the Basie band was like going before the Supreme Court, you know? “Wow man I don’t know if this is going to work, man, this isn’t Basie. No, it’s not going to work, toss it.” It took me years, like what? Man. But the Basie band, that’s how they kept their sound. They were very strict as far as not letting just anything be played by them. And so I learned the Basie sound, the equation for what is a Count Basie arrangement. Because Count Basie wasn’t an arranger, actually he was hardly a human composer — a handful of tunes that were made into arrangements. His arrangers were like Frank Foster and Thad Jones and Jim Mundy, Nestico and I’m leaving out somebody.
Neal Hefti. All these and then a few others. Quincy Jones.

Ernie Wilkins, yeah, oh man, Ernie Wilkins. So those were the people who formed the Basie sound. And when they brought in an arrangement to the band, oh it was even worse then. Because that’s when Basie was alive it was in its heyday. And that’s when Basie would kind of carve up the arrangement and say “that section right there, on the bridge © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

there, the horns you all lay out, I’m gonna take that.” Oh big old — you know it could be like this thick orchestrated thing, you know, all this counterpoint, all this other stuff, and Basie says “cut it out, I’m gonna take that.” What?
And can you just picture after all that. I mean here you are like yeah, Basie’s band playing my stuff. And then it’s like yeah, but.
Yeah. Throw that out, I’m gonna take that. And after he would do his surgical thing on an arrangement then he would say okay. Now that’s Basie. And the arrangement would be what it is.
